label: JavaScript (QuickJS-ng)

versions.engine: QuickJS-ng 0.17.0 (interpreter, no JIT), built from the pinned source tarball
versions.flags: identical CMake configuration both sides: Release, -O2 -DNDEBUG, QJS_BUILD_LIBC=ON, no mimalloc, no static CLI, no reactor; wasm adds only what QuickJS's own WASI CMake branch adds (2 MiB stack, wasi-emulated process-clocks and signal)

transforms: build time: the line globalThis.process = { argv: ["qjs", ...scriptArgs] }; is inserted after the first line ("use strict") of every languages/javascript/<b>.js to produce /app/js/<b>.js, run identically by all three columns (QuickJS has no process.argv; process.argv is the only Node-only API the 18 sources use)
asymmetries: this is QuickJS-ng, an interpreter, NOT V8: the ratio is NOT comparable to the matrix Node/V8 JavaScript cell (a speculative JIT); V8 cannot be compiled to wasm
the native qjs links glibc dynamically (glibc malloc, libm), the wasm module links wasi-libc statically (dlmalloc, wasi libm)
native clang is the official LLVM 23.1.0 release, wasm clang is wasi-sdk 34's build of 23.1.0 (different commits of the same release)
stack: native uses the process stack, the wasm build uses QuickJS's WASI default of 2 MiB; the benchmarks recurse shallowly, far from either limit

value representation: QuickJS uses NaN-boxing (64-bit JSValue) on 32-bit targets (quickjs.h: JS_NAN_BOXING when INTPTR_MAX < INT64_MAX), so the wasm32 build boxes values differently from the native 64-bit build (16-byte tagged struct)
